name: Northridge Lumber Camp
summary: Scarlet Crusade guards hold Northridge Lumber Camp, an active, fortified mill in the hills near Hearthglen. Its timber feeds nearby strongholds, and the Alliance and Horde seek ways to cripple the Crusade’s supply.

sections.title: Fueling the Crusade
sections.body: Scarlet Crusade workers fell and process timber at Northridge Lumber Camp, despite the plague in the surrounding forests. The mill lies down the road from Hearthglen, in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands. Its wood builds fortifications, repairs watchtowers, and sustains the Crusade’s war effort in Lordaeron. Guards and laborers garrison the camp in force, defending it from the Scourge and trespassers.

sections.title: Target for Sabotage
sections.body: Hearthglen depends on Northridge Lumber Camp for timber to maintain its defenses. That need makes the mill a target for outside forces. Alliance commanders and Horde scouts know a direct assault on fortified Crusade positions would cost dearly. So their agents seek quieter ways to sabotage the operation, such as releasing wood-boring termites into the lumber stores and spoiling the Crusade’s supplies from within.

faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade controls and operates Northridge Lumber Camp. Its guards and laborers harvest timber for nearby strongholds.

faq.q: Why is this lumber mill important?
faq.answer: The mill supplies timber for the Scarlet Crusade’s fortifications and watchtowers. That wood supports its nearby strongholds and war effort in Lordaeron.

faq.q: Why do the Alliance and Horde want to sabotage it?
faq.answer: The Alliance and Horde see the aggressive, fanatical Scarlet Crusade as a threat in the Plaguelands. Sabotage can weaken its lumber supplies and defenses without the cost of a direct assault.

faq.q: Who ran the mill before the Third War?
faq.answer: Before the Kingdom of Lordaeron fell to the Scourge, local civilian families lived and worked at the mill. It was a quiet regional enterprise.

angles.text: As an Alliance scout, you face the Scarlet Crusade’s violent xenophobia during reconnaissance and operations in northern Lordaeron, though the Crusade claims to fight the undead.
As a Forsaken or Horde ally, you can weaken Hearthglen by disrupting the Crusade’s lumber supply and pressuring its zealots toward their strongholds.
